scenario.symptoms: Users see friend suggestions for people they unfriended months ago. The daily graph feature batch finished 36 hours late and serving still reads yesterday’s precomputed lists.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Online serving reads static batch outputs from object storage without versioning tied to graph snapshot time. Incremental friendship deletes are not applied until the next full batch.

incident.headline: Serving stale batch recommendations after delayed graph pipeline

agenda.goal: Keep PYMK lists fresh despite heavy batch computation.
agenda.opener: Suggestions include people users unfriended—how do batch and online paths stay consistent?

evidence.strong: Hybrid batch + incremental updates, snapshot versioning, filter deletes on read, SLA alerts on batch lag.
evidence.adequate: Faster batch only without online corrections.
evidence.weak: Daily batch as sole source with no invalidation.

probes: Which signals must be real-time vs batch?
How do you merge incremental deletes into cached lists?
hints: Apply negative filters from a realtime blocklist.
agenda.referenceFix: Publish batch lists with version timestamps, maintain realtime unfriend/block filter at serve time, and fall back to on-demand small graph lookups when batch lag exceeds SLA.

scenario.symptoms: A user who blocked their ex still received a ‘people you may know’ card with that person’s photo. Support escalations cite harassment concerns.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Candidate generation uses mutual friends but does not subtract block/mute edges before ranking. Privacy filters run only in messaging, not recommendations.

incident.headline: Block graph edges omitted from PYMK filtering

agenda.goal: Never recommend users across block or privacy boundaries.
agenda.opener: A blocked person showed up in PYMK—where must privacy filters run?

evidence.strong: Filter blocked/muted/deleted accounts before rank and after batch merge, with tests and audit logs.

misconceptions.pattern: Hiding suggestions only in the UI.
misconceptions.challenge: Can a API client or notification still expose the blocked profile?

probes: How do you filter at batch scale efficiently?
hints: Treat block list as hard constraint, not ranking feature.
Join block bitmap early in candidate generation.
agenda.referenceFix: Apply block/mute/deactivated filters in candidate generation and final rerank, store per-user deny sets in low-latency store, and add compliance tests for blocked pairs.

nuggets.title: Realtime graph features lag social actions

scenario.symptoms: New users see empty PYMK for 48 hours while veterans get instant suggestions. Realtime friend accept events queue behind a backlog, so online features miss fresh edges.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Streaming feature updater shares Kafka consumer group with heavy batch backfill jobs that starve realtime partition consumption.

incident.headline: Backfill competes with realtime graph feature updates

agenda.goal: Update PYMK features within minutes of new social graph actions.
agenda.opener: New friendships take days to affect PYMK—what pipeline issue causes that lag?

evidence.strong: Separate consumer groups/topics for backfill vs realtime, priority processing, lag alerts, and cold-start fallback heuristics.

probes: How do you bootstrap features for brand-new users?
What SLA do you target for accept-friend events?
hints: Never share one consumer group between backfill and live.
agenda.referenceFix: Isolate realtime graph updater with dedicated partitions, throttle backfill separately, alert on consumer lag, and serve heuristic PYMK until features warm.
